title: Microsoft Teams: invite people to register for events by email
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's rollout notice, custom-domain restriction and existing attendee-access controls. The sending-domain path reaches the correct settings page but should continue to the option that enables the custom domain.

claims.claim: Organisers of Teams events with registration enabled can send email invitations containing a registration link.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is expanding the Invite to register experience for Teams events with registration enabled. Organizers can select people to receive an email invitation with a link to register for the event.

claims.quote: No special preparation is required. However, if your tenant does not have a custom domain configured for M365 notifications, this capability will be restricted due to spam concerns.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to configure their custom domain for Microsoft 365 notifications to allow full use.
claims.quote: Admins should configure their custom domain for M365 notifications to allow full use of this feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified what the missing-domain restriction looks like to an organiser.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "Invite to register" custom domain restrictions price meter; "Teams" "Invite to register" "restrictions". Read MC1537353 and Learn manage-email-communications; neither describes the restriction's mechanics.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe Invite to register itself beyond the supplied record and notice.
claims.quote: Searched: "Invite to register"; "microsoftteams" "invite" "register". Read manage-email-communications, set-up-events, events-licensing and the Support Events app registration page; none describes this invitation experience.

claims.claim: Teams events documentation recommends a custom sending domain to improve email deliverability.
claims.quote: Set up a custom domain for event emails (recommended) ... Increase email deliverability and reduce spam classification.

claims.claim: Teams events documentation says a custom sending domain reduces spam classification.
claims.quote: Increase email deliverability and reduce spam classification.

claims.claim: Without a custom domain, event emails come from Microsoft-provided addresses that might be less recognisable.
claims.quote: While events can function without a custom domain, emails are sent from Microsoft-provided addresses that might be less recognizable to recipients.

claims.claim: Microsoft says a custom domain builds greater trust for external audiences receiving invitations.
claims.quote: Build greater trust for external audiences receiving invitations and updates.

claims.claim: The sending-domain setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Send email notifications from your domain.
claims.quote: On the Organization profile page, select Send email notifications from your domain. ... In the Send email notifications from your domain page, select Use a custom send-from domain address.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and the matching table path to 'Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Send email notifications from your domain > Use a custom send-from domain address'. The current path stops on the correct page before its enabling control.

claims.claim: No automation operation for the Microsoft 365 notification sending-domain setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Send email notifications from your domain" PowerShell Graph API; "send-from" "domain" "Graph" notification settings; "custom send-from" "PowerShell". Read the domain-setting page; Graph emailSettings search result covers Lifecycle Workflows, not this setting.

claims.claim: The notification sending-domain setting is opt-in.
claims.quote: This setting is an opt-in setting that allows the Microsoft 365 system administrators to select a verified domain within the tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The notification sending-domain setting can take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: The setting can take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Only domains registered within the tenant can be used for the notification sending-domain setting.
claims.quote: Only domains registered within your tenant can be used.

claims.claim: Ownership of the selected domain must be verified.
claims.quote: Domain ownership must be verified through the existing add domains process within Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams supports the tenant's Microsoft 365 notification sending-domain setting.
claims.quote: Supported products ... The following products currently support this feature: ... Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: When configured, event notification emails can use the verified custom domain selected by administrators.
claims.quote: admins can configure Teams events email notifications to be sent from a verified custom domain instead of Microsoft default addresses.

claims.claim: The webinar-size attendance setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events up to 1k attendees dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests configures the attendee-access restriction for events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization to attend events with up to 1,000 attendees created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -EventAccessType EveryoneInCompanyExcludingGuests

claims.claim: The large-audience attendance setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests configures attendance for large-audience events.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The first attendee-access policy setting governs who can attend events up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, created by organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls who can attend events with up to 1,000 attendees (such as webinars) created by organizers with this policy.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; controls[2].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The second attendee-access policy setting governs who can attend large-audience events, such as town halls, created by organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls who can attend events optimized for large audiences (such as town halls) created by organizers with this policy.

claims.claim: Who can attend events up to 1k attendees defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone.

claims.claim: Who can attend events optimized for a large audience defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone.

claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI switch or PowerShell parameter to turn Invite to register on or off is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "Invite to register" licensing policy disable; "Teams" "Invite to register" "policy" "Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy". Read set-up-events, manage-email-communications and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax and registration parameters; no dedicated invitation switch found.
